mentions.name: Porting Ruby to Fil-C
mentions.description: This project ports the Ruby programming language to Fil-C. Ruby's codebase uses a `typedef uintptr_t VALUE` that can hold a heap pointer, a tagged Ruby value, or any integer fitting in uintptr_t, while Fil-C doesn't allow pointers to be carried as integers without losing their capabilities. Since VALUE variables are also used for integer and bit math, the port requires a nontrivial patch to Ruby and is about 70% complete.
mentions.problem: Fil-C doesn't allow pointers to be carried as integers (doing so makes pointers lose their capabilities), but Ruby's uintptr_t VALUE type conflates heap pointers, tagged values, and integers, so changing it isn't as simple as switching to a pointer type.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Porting Ruby to Fil-C

It's very interesting because the Ruby codebase uses a `typedef uintptr_t VALUE` type to mean any of the following:

- A pointer to the heap

- A Ruby tagged value (which may be a pointer to the heap)

- Any integer value that fits in `uintptr_t`
